fig1_angular_pattern.svg: Normalized angular shape of each multipole potential at fixed radius (theta from the symmetry axis): the monopole is isotropic, the dipole has the cos(theta) two-lobe pattern, and the linear quadrupole shows the P2 four-lobe pattern, all evaluated from the module's potential functions.
fig2_radial_falloff.svg: On-axis magnitude of the monopole, dipole, and quadrupole potentials versus distance (log-log). The straight lines have slopes -1, -2, -3, so each higher multipole decays one extra power of r faster -- the 1/r^(l+1) hierarchy that lets the nearest non-zero moment dominate far away.
